commits.summary: Verification queue priorities: move committed jobs up or down later, and run only the top of the queue
commits.body: Job files are committed with the change they verify and not edited after, so a job's own priority was fixed at submit time and no job set one. verification/priorities.json now holds priorities by job id, each with a reason, set with 'pipeline.py prioritize ID... --priority N --reason TEXT' (--clear, no ids lists them). 'run --min-priority N' runs only the jobs at N or above and leaves the rest pending; 'status' lists pending jobs in start order with their priorities and says when priorities.json has uncommitted changes.

commits.summary: A relative --jbmc path is found, and --details prints the statement and the time under a verdict
commits.body:
A --jbmc path given relative to the current directory (bin/jbmc) passed the availability check, which runs where the command is started, then failed as 'JBMC produced no verdict: no output', since JBMC runs in the work directory. jbmc::executable makes such a path absolute where both drivers build their JBMC runs; a bare name is still looked up on PATH. Reproduced first with the previous binary on a one-line class, then fixed; unit test a_relative_jbmc_path_is_made_absolute_and_a_bare_name_is_left_to_path and CLI test a_relative_jbmc_path_is_found_from_the_current_directory on the real JBMC.

--details on prove and equivalence (lib/src/details.rs) prints, under the verdict, what --json holds as stated and search: the statement (domain, each assumption with its basis, what is observed, bounds, models, checker with solver and gap mode, confirmation, vacuity) and where the time went (the check's total, the driver's steps, and each checker run with its purpose, stage, ending, phase shares and formula size). The default report is unchanged. CLI test details_print_the_statement_and_where_the_time_went; lib/README.md documents both.

All Rust tests pass: 148 unit, 6 conformance, 62 integration. In the full run, on a loaded machine (635 s), the_tools_own_checker_agrees_with_jbmc_on_integer_proofs failed at its first assertion (the Pricing native regression proof, time-dependent, as recorded before); it passed alone in 16 s.

commits.summary: Benchmark group 2 reviewed by the user: the midpoint regression's scope tightened, the checksum property's note corrected
commits.body:
The user reviewed the 13 group 2 cases (lib/benchmark/corpus.json) against their sources and code, case by case; this closes the benchmark's departure 'no person reviewed group 2's properties' (5a). Eleven were accepted as they were.

real/midpoint/fix-confined: the scope was 'low < 0 || high < low || low + high < 0', wider than the claim needs; for any two ints whose wrapped sum is not negative, (low + high) / 2 == (low + high) >>> 1, so it is now 'low + high < 0', a stronger claim with the same expected verdict, in corpus.json and Reference.java, with its 'why' corrected. real/checksum/broken-property: its 'why' now says the throws clause catches the bug and that the assertion only covers the empty range.

Verified inline on the own checker under strict (run.py --groups 2, 20 s deadline): midpoint/fix-confined verified in 0.11 s and held on the JVM over 121,136 random inputs; all checksum and midpoint cases correct; test_run.py 17 pass. Job 20261106-102624 runs at its own commit, so its table has the previous scope.

commits.summary: The own checker makes a division or product of equal operands one value: a functional-consistency lemma before any circuit is built
commits.body:
The own checker leaves divisions and multiplications to the solver as fresh bits under facts, and shares one only when its operand terms are identical. Two operations on equal values written differently (Math.abs(hash) % n and (hash & 0x7fffffff) % n, for a hash that is not negative) were separate unknowns, so the solver answered them differently, each model was refined, both 32-bit dividers were built, and the solver was left proving two dividers equivalent: benchmark case real/bucket/fix-confined ran out of time (over 100 s; 20 s deadline: 2 of 2 divisions built, 53,649 clauses).

Now, when a model gives two operations of one kind and width equal operands (a product's in either order) but different results, bits.rs adds the lemma (a1 == a2 && b1 == b2) -> (q1 == q2 && r1 == r2) and solves again, before refining any operation (Blaster::inconsistent_pair, add_congruence; the engine's solve loop). The lemma holds of every real operation, so it rules out no real execution; for a division by zero, whose bits nothing reads, it only picks equal values.

commits.summary: Confirming a proof that rests on contracts: under --confirm, JBMC applies the own checker's contracts at the same calls and proves it again
commits.body:
Under --engine auto --confirm, a proof of the own checker that rests on contracts for gaps (--gaps advised) was not sent to JBMC: the confirmation was not-asked, with the reason 'JBMC cannot apply' a contract, untrue since JBMC applies contracts by rewriting call sites (step 4c, part two). equivalence::confirm now takes the contracts (ConfirmContracts: the gap setting, the directories whose call sites are rewritten, the class path, a directory): it reads JBMC's goto program, applies the same contracts with jbmc_contracts::apply, runs JBMC on the rewritten class path, holds its proof to what it still approximates under the own checker's gap mode, and settles the contract records. A confirmed proof says it rests on the same contracts, by id. Gaps assumed under --gaps assume stay not-asked; a gap JBMC has that no contract closes gives no verdict.

A confirmation checks the reasoning given the contracts, not the contracts, whose evidence (proved, tested, trusted) the verdict states. Both drivers pass the contracts; lib/README.md describes it, and the sound-verdicts brief records the user's decisions and the group 2 review as done.

commits.summary: The end-of-turn hook leaves a session that wrote no transcript unmarked, so check stops warning about it
commits.body: Claude Code can fire the Stop or SessionEnd hook with a transcript_path for a session that never wrote a transcript (one opened and closed with no message, say). The hook marked the session as having turns not yet sent to Langfuse before reading anything, then failed on the missing file, so the mark stayed and check warned about it until 'sync.py langfuse' cleared it by hand: four such sessions on 2026-11-05/06 (28b02734, 87db5b5f, d10805f9, cdc1176b), none with a transcript in any project folder. The hook now returns before marking when the transcript does not exist, and logs one line.

commits.summary: Pipeline jobs apply git-format patches: git in a job no longer takes this repository for the job's, and a skipped file fails the patch stage
commits.body:
A pipeline job's export and build.py's patched copies live under verification/.state/work, inside this repository's tree. There, git apply reads a git-format patch's paths (diff --git) from this repository's top level, skips every file outside the copy and still exits 0. Since change myrqmxqq (2026-11-05 18:54), which keeps each attempt's copy in the job's work directory, every pipeline run of an example with a git-format patch ran on the unpatched code: 25 examples (110-119, 128-139, 147-149). Job 20261106-073804 found it: examples 128-131 and 134 gave no verdict ('class not found: net.terminalvalue.crosscut.kafka.Batch', a class the patch adds). An example expected to verify would have compared the unpatched code with itself and matched its expectation. No collected result is affected: nothing was collected after that change.

The runner now sets GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES to the work directory's parent in every step's environment, which also covers the jobs queued at older commits, whose build.py has no guard. build.py's new apply_patch (both apply sites) sets the same, runs git apply --verbose, and fails the stage on any 'Skipped patch' line.

commits.summary: The JBMC patch-queue draft is rewritten as engine-priorities.md: stock JBMC, better staging, wider native coverage
commits.body: An outside review of the repository at 6cea609e (kept verbatim as llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities-review.md) read the raw benchmark results of job 20261106-102624 and the JBMC jobs' outputs, and changes the draft's direction. Its figures were rechecked against lib/benchmark/results.json. Case by case, the own checker alone decides 10 cases correctly under strict and JBMC alone 3. The own checker was faster on all 98 cases both decided correctly. JBMC's [0:20] and [-100000:100000] stages take about 30 s of binary search's 58.6 s and of 141's 65.2 s, and 15 s of floor-mod's 15.5 s, where the full range finds its counterexample in 0.25 s. The JBMC phase table counts time twice: CBMC times Runtime Post-process inside Runtime Solver, and phases.rs adds one to encoding and the other to solving (held/reverse's phases add up to 22.0 s against 15.9 s of wall time). The three cases only JBMC wins are all application <clinit>s.\n\nThe draft, renamed llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md and still not a brief, now plans: (1) exclusive JBMC phases, solver identity recorded, a strict rerun saving gap_table.py's output; (2) a job comparing today's staged search, full range first, and one tightly budgeted stage; (3) application class initializers in the own checker, counted before implementing, then a native/JBMC coverage inventory; (4) the root cause of the two JBMC witnesses that don't reproduce (caught/1, nestedHandler/1); (5) captured incremental queries and a narrow SAT interface before solver experiments; (6) contracts for example 071's two property proofs. The fork candidates are deferred. Old instructions are dropped rather than kept, at the user's request. Links in sound-verdicts.md and lib/benchmark/README.md point at the new file; the README notes the overcount. Documents only, nothing run.

commits.summary: engine-priorities.md records the user's answers on staging, class initializers and solvers
commits.body: Three of the draft's open questions were settled with the user on 2026-11-06. If full range first wins, only JBMC's staging default changes; the own checker keeps its cheap per-path stages. Class-initializer support starts with a count of the gaps over the recorded examples and the apps, then a scope that leans toward the semantics that occur most. For solvers, Bitwuzla is preferred, as a path to word-level obligations on top of CaDiCaL, and other experiments stay in only where the gain is more than incremental. Phase 2 also now says that lib/src/shrink.rs already shrinks any engine's witness through the interpreter, so full range first doesn't mean large witnesses. The order of the phases is still open, to be reviewed before the brief is written. Documents only.

commits.summary: engine-priorities.md folds example 071's work into Phase 3 as JDK models for Enum.<init>, List.of and List.copyOf
commits.body: Decided with the user on 2026-11-06. Example 071's first two property proofs, and 013's, reach JBMC stubs for Enum.<init>(String, int), List.of and List.copyOf, all called through Quorum's Decision type and its enums, so strict turns those proofs into no verdict. Contracts can't close these well: with object parameters they can only be trusted, which is below the proved-or-tested bar for CI, and they can be false in general (List.of throws on a null element). So Phase 3 now adds exact models in lib/models instead: Enum.<init> sets name and ordinal; the immutable list keeps null rejection, refusal of changes, and copyOf's identity. The check is 071 and 013 rerun under strict. The separate Phase 6 is removed. Contracts over complex objects, and other ways of verifying them, move to a new Deferred section to revisit in a later loop. Also corrects the evidence: 071 reaches all three stubs, as 013 does. Documents only.

commits.summary: engine-priorities.md becomes a loop brief, for the user's final review
commits.body: The working draft is now a brief for llm-dlc/tools/feature-loop.sh, not yet approved. It has six phases in the order proposed with the user: (1) exclusive JBMC phases, the SAT backend recorded in every result, and the Bitwuzla build queued early; (2) a JBMC staging-policy option, and one benchmark job that both reruns the corpus with corrected phases and compares three policies, with JBMC's default following its evidence; (3) the root cause of the two JBMC witnesses that don't reproduce; (4) a strict job on both engines over the 41 recorded JBMC examples, saving gap_table.py's output, and class initializers counted by shape, giving a coverage inventory; (5) class initializers in the own checker to the counted scope, plus models for Enum.<init>, List.of and List.copyOf, checked by rerunning 071 and 013 under strict; (6) query transcripts, a narrow solver interface, and a job comparing CaDiCaL with Bitwuzla, bit-blasted and word-level, ending in a recommendation rather than a migration. It adds working rules, a Done-when table, Deferred (the fork, trusted contracts over objects, a word-level migration), the settled decisions, Progress, Loop settings (this session, Opus 5.5, high effort) and Loop until. The evidence section is unchanged. Links in sound-verdicts.md are reworded. Documents only.

commits.summary: A stopped feature loop continues by running the same command again
commits.body: feature-loop.sh's instruction for a brief used to send the session to the next piece of work that 'this run's earlier commits' had not done. A restart sets a new starting change, so after one that list is empty, and nothing made the session look at changes an interrupted cycle left in the working copy, which the next commit could then sweep into unrelated work. Each cycle now first runs jj status, and finishes, verifies and commits a change left there (or says in the commit why it sets it aside). It then takes the next piece of work by the brief's Progress section, which carries over between runs, as well as this run's commits. The header comment and llm-dlc/README.md say that the restart is the same command, and to leave no other work uncommitted when starting. Verified with bash -n and by expanding the instruction for engine-priorities.md and reading it.

commits.summary: A feature-loop cycle finishes only its own interrupted work and keeps other sessions' files out of its commit
commits.body: Following the previous commit, a cycle treated any change in the working copy as its own interrupted work. That would be wrong while the verification loop or another session has files there uncommitted, and sync.py commit commits the whole working copy. Each cycle now runs jj status and judges what a change is. One that belongs to the brief's current step, by its Progress section or the session's own last turn, is finished, verified and committed, and that is the cycle's piece of work. Anything else is another session's: it is left alone, never finished, reverted or discarded, and kept out of the cycle's commit by moving it below and back, as step 5 of .claude/skills/run-verification/SKILL.md already does the other way round. The header comment and llm-dlc/README.md are updated to match. Verified with bash -n and by expanding the instruction for engine-priorities.md and reading it.

commits.summary: A push uploads each session's current log, so a session that made no commit is published too
commits.body: Session 3048539b, opened on 2026-10-31 and left empty (a 0-byte transcript), had its manifest committed, but its only log was never uploaded: cmd_upload uploaded the logs commits and subagents point at, and that session has neither. On any other machine, where traces/*/logs/ is not checked out, check then fails with 'log e3b0c44298fc is neither stored locally nor uploaded'. At push (include_at), cmd_upload now also uploads each session's current log, the one its committed manifest names. It is scanned like any other, so nothing is published without the redaction check. Only 3048539b had such a log; this session's unuploaded logs belong to commits not pushed yet. New test test_a_push_uploads_the_current_log_of_a_session_that_made_no_commit: a plain upload leaves it alone, and the push's upload puts it on the CDN and records its URL. 102 tests in test_performance.py and 49 in test_review/test_metrics pass.

commits.summary: The engine-priorities brief runs as two parallel streams in jj workspaces, reconciled by its own loop
commits.body:
The plan of llm-dlc/loops/engine-priorities.md is split along the line between the engines: engine-priorities-jbmc.md (phases 1a, 1b, 2, 3, 4a: the JBMC adapter and the measurements) and engine-priorities-native.md (1c, 4b, 5, 6: the own checker, its models and the solver), each a loop of its own (feature-loop.sh engines-jbmc / engines-native) with its own session, its own Progress, a 2.5 GB cap, and its own jj workspace and branch. The stream briefs name the files each owns and the shared ones where changes are additions only. The main brief gains a Streams section: how to start them, and the reconcile procedure that is now its own loop's first work (record each stream's last turns, copy its logs, merge, regenerate the trace index, fold Progress, forget the workspaces), followed by 4c and the rest.

To make that work: feature-loop.sh names its systemd scope after the loop (feature-loop-NAME.scope), so two loops can run at once, and reads '- memory: SIZE' and '- workspace: NAME' from a brief's Loop settings, refusing to run outside that workspace. verification/pipeline.py's run and status read jobs from @- of every jj workspace, not just their own, so a stream's job runs at its commit without a merge (queue_revs, queued_jobs). Docs: llm-dlc/README.md (parallel loops), verification/README.md, the run-verification skill's memory budget.

commits.summary: run-streams.sh starts a brief's parallel streams in one terminal, each forked from the compacted planning session
commits.body:
llm-dlc/tools/run-streams.sh engines, run from the default workspace, sets up and runs the engine-priorities streams. The first time, it compacts the brief's own session (the conversation that planned the streams) once and adds the jj workspaces ../REPO-jbmc and ../REPO-native from @-. It then runs feature-loop.sh engines-jbmc and engines-native from their workspaces side by side, each line prefixed with its stream. Each runs in its own process group, so Ctrl-C is passed to both loops, which record the interruption. Running it again continues them without compacting or forking again. If the planning session's transcript is missing (it ran on another machine), it says where to copy it.

feature-loop.sh reads a new '- fork: SESSION' brief setting. A session with no transcript yet starts as a fork of that one (claude --resume PARENT --fork-session --session-id ID), in a first turn with tools and project settings off. The parent's transcript is copied into the workspace's project directory for the fork and removed after it, so the repo's hooks never sync it there, where it would be published as a second copy. Both stream briefs fork from 3761db96 and drop their 2.5 GB caps (they will run on a larger machine, cvm, under the default 3.5 GB each). The main brief, llm-dlc/README.md and the run-verification skill describe it.

commits.summary: copy-session.sh moves a session to another machine, and the reconcile loop starts fresh with a map of the streams' work
commits.body:
llm-dlc/tools/copy-session.sh HOST SESSION (id or unique prefix), run after closing a session, moves it to another machine. It refuses a session that is live (a claude process names it, or its transcript changed in the last minute) and publishes with sync.py push --bookmark main (--no-push skips that). It copies the transcript and the session's directory into HOST's Claude Code project directory for the repo, under a temporary name with a checksum check, and refuses to overwrite a different transcript there. Then it moves the local transcript to ~/.claude/moved-sessions/, so the session goes on on one machine only: a push from here republishes every session it finds and would roll back one that grew on HOST (--keep-local keeps it). It exists to take the planning session 3761db96 to cvm, where run-streams.sh forks the streams from it.

The engine-priorities brief's own loop, which merges the streams, now starts from a fresh session (c2bd9df4) instead of resuming the planning session. Its Streams section gains a table of where everything is for a session that saw none of it: the planning session and its summary, how the streams ran (workspaces, scopes, forked sessions, branches), their commits, Progress on their branches, run records in their workspaces' loop-summaries, published summaries, logs and jobs. Reconcile step 2 now refuses to commit a stream's uncommitted work, since that means an interrupted cycle. run-streams.sh takes the session to compact and fork from the stream briefs' '- fork:' (which must agree), no longer from the main brief.

Verified with fake ssh and scp running against a local fake remote home. Each case behaved as intended: refusing a just-written transcript and one a claude process names, copying the transcript and its directory with matching checksums, retiring the local copy with a .moved note, refusing a different remote transcript, and --keep-local. run-streams.sh rerun in a throwaway jj repo with a fake claude: a missing planning transcript stops it, otherwise one compact and two forks from 3761db96, then both loops.

This session's three commits were also rebased onto main, which claude-vm had moved by two commits (installer changes and a trace record). The only conflicts were in generated trace files (llm-dlc/traces/README.md, metrics.json), resolved by taking main's side and regenerated by this commit.

commits.summary: Accept finding 4a9c05db: the laptop's hostname kept as its machine name in verification results
transfer-session.sh (was copy-session.sh) also brings the other machine's repo to the pushed main
commits.body: The script that moves a session to another machine now does everything before run-streams.sh. It fetches here and refuses unless this repo is on top of the remote main, since another machine may have pushed meanwhile. Then it pushes, copies the transcript and moves the local copy aside as before. Last, on HOST over ssh (in a login shell, where jj lives), it fetches and starts a new change on main. It refuses, changing nothing, if HOST has commits not on main or uncommitted work. Uncommitted changes to regenerated trace files alone are dropped. It then confirms HOST is at the pushed commit and runs sync.py check there. llm-dlc/README.md describes it.

commits.summary: Record session traces
commits.body: Brings the published traces up to this point: conversation that came after a session's last commit, and sessions with no commit of their own.

commits.summary: run-streams.sh runs a brief's whole loop unattended: streams, jobs, then the merge
commits.body:
llm-dlc/tools/run-streams.sh engines now needs a person only at the end. After the compact, forks and workspaces, it starts verification-loop.sh (unless one already runs for this repo) so the loops' jobs are run, collected and committed. It runs both streams' loops and supervises each. When every stream is finished, it runs the brief's own loop (feature-loop.sh engines, the merge, in its fresh session) the same way, then stops the verification loop and exits.

The supervisor reads a status line that each brief now ends its Progress with: '- Status: working', 'waiting on jobs ID ...', 'done' or 'blocked: ...'. All three engine-priorities briefs carry the rule and start at 'working'. A loop waiting on jobs is run again once each job's result is collected under verification/results/, polling every RUN_STREAMS_POLL seconds (300) and giving up as blocked after RUN_STREAMS_JOB_WAIT (12 h). Done or blocked, it is finished, and a blocked stream is merged with what it committed. A stop with no such status is retried once, then counted as blocked; so is one claiming to wait on jobs that are already back. On a restart, finished loops are skipped and waiting ones wait first. verification-loop.sh gains a stop on SIGUSR1, which lets the run under way finish. The brief's Streams and Reconciling text and llm-dlc/README.md describe it.

Verified with a dry run in a throwaway jj repo, with a fake claude that sets status lines and commits and a fake verification loop that collects a job after a few seconds. In order: one compact and two forks; jbmc waited on its job, picked up when it was collected and finished; native finished; the merge loop ran and finished; the verification loop stopped on SIGUSR1; exit 0. A restart skipped the finished stream. Ctrl-C mid-cycle gave exit 130, both stream loops recorded the interruption, and no process or scope was left. The verification-loop detection first matched the test shell's own command line; it now needs a bash running the script with the repo as its working directory.
